Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Town, shops & places

Lisbon noun

Renaissance

Braun & Hogenberg, Civitates orbis terrarum I, 1572, “vulgo Lisbona”

1Lisbōna: long o. The long ō keeps the stress of Portuguese Lisboa on that syllable, by the convention for modern names (Olisīpō has a long ō in the same place). Ruling: Modern place names: a convention for their vowels.

Lisbōna1, Lisbōnae f.

noun, first declension

The form the libellī use; Olisīpō is just as good. Cities and small places take no preposition: Lisbōnam volābimus, Lisbōnae sumus, Sintrā (from Sintra); countries take one: in Lūsitāniam, in Lūsitāniā.

Other words

  • Olisīpō, Olisīpōnis m. — the ancient name

    noun, third declension · classical · Pliny, NH 4.117; L&S Olisipo, with ī

    The ancient name, which many Latin speakers use today.

See also Portugal, Tagus, Alfama, Gare do Oriente, Parque das Nações.

SourcesLewis & Short: Olisipo

Georg Braun and Frans Hogenberg, Civitates orbis terrarum I (1572), as cited.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
